title: content/combat_caps.json
description: 05 §1-2 — the combat simulator's constants. 05 §1.1: 'every cap above lives in res://data/combat_caps.json'; 05 §2's hero base stat block carries its own 📐 TUNABLE. The file also holds 05 §4.1's ward pool cap, 05 §4's two mitigation dials and 11 §4.3's pvpMaxFightSeconds, each of which names combat_caps.json in its own section. 🔒 It lives under content/ rather than tuning/: doc 21's catalogue names exactly sixteen tuning files and a seventeenth is a bug, and these are balance and simulator constants, not economy dials that the economy simulator sweeps. The same ruling was enforced in code by TunableMarkerAudit.NonEconomyDataFiles until the 📐 audit was removed; it is now a convention this comment is the only record of. ⚠️ The citation is deliberately written without a section marker — that catalogue section is itself a recorded out-of-scope 📐 baseline entry, and citing it here would close an entry this change did not close.

ratio01.description: 05 §1 — a stat the table types as 0..1. multipleOf pins it to 05 §1.1's 4-decimal-place form: a cap that is not itself rounded puts an unrounded value into every stat it binds, and this is the difference between a content-build failure and a runtime throw out of Core.

baseStatCurve.description: 05 §2 — one stat's base value as base + perLevel * L. A stat 05 §2 states as a single constant carries perLevel 0. Both coefficients are pinned to 05 §1.1's 4-decimal-place form.

caps.description: 05 §1 — the five capped stats and nothing else. Keyed by 18 §2.1 StatId name: 05 §1's LS is LIFESTEAL. 🔒 additionalProperties is false and all five are required, so a cap that is dropped or renamed fails the build rather than silently becoming 'uncapped'. The remaining combat stats are absent because 05 §1 caps none of them; absence here means uncapped, which is the only meaning 05 authorises. Each bound is an UPPER bound — 05 states no lower bound for any stat and none is invented (16 R6). DR_PCT left this set with 16 D46: it is a damage-taken multiplier now, bounded below in floors.

BLOCK.description: 05 §1 — Block, capped at 0.60. A block halves the hit.

floors.description: 16 D46 — the one authored floor. DR_PCT is the damage-taken multiplier (base 1.00, consumed bare), so 05 §1's 'at most 60% reduction' cap re-expresses as a LOWER bound on the multiplier: 1.0 − 0.6 = 0.4. 🔒 additionalProperties is false and DR_PCT is required, so the floor can neither vanish silently nor gain uninvented company (16 R6). STAT_CAP_OVERRIDE's STAT_MAX rewrites ceilings only and never touches a floor.

DR_PCT.description: 16 D46 — the damage-taken multiplier's lower bound: 1.0 − 0.6 = 0.4.

heroBaseStats.description: 05 §2 — the hero's Base(stat) curve, which 18 §8 step 4 adds flat modifiers to. 🔒 All fourteen combat stats of 05 §1 are required: 05 §2 rules that 'every actor — hero and enemy alike — carries a complete 14-stat block with these defaults. An unstated stat is a bug, not a zero.' Making a stat optional here would turn that ruling back into a silent zero, and HEAL_PCT is the case that proves it — its base is 1.0 because it multiplies ALL healing received, so a defaulted 0 disables every heal in the game.

legendLevelMin.description: 05 §2 — 'where L = Legend Level (1..200)', the lower bound.

legendLevelMax.description: 05 §2 — 'where L = Legend Level (1..200)', the upper bound. The curve is not authored beyond it. ⚠️ That this is >= legendLevelMin is NOT expressible here: the validator's keyword set is closed and holds no if/then, and a cross-key comparison is not a JSON Schema assertion. HeroBaseCurve.From enforces it, and that is stated so the gap is on the record rather than assumed covered.

stats.description: 05 §2 — one row per combat stat, in the order 05 §1's table presents them. _doc is permitted here as it is on every other block in this file, so a per-block note is not a validation failure.

DEF.description: 05 §2 — DEF = 15 + 3 * L. 05 §1: mitigation, not flat subtraction.

DMG_PCT.description: 05 §2 / 16 D46 — DMG% = 1.00: a multiplier stat consumed bare, so its base is the identity.

DR_PCT.description: 05 §2 / 16 D46 — DR% = 1.00: the damage-taken multiplier's identity.

HEAL_PCT.description: 05 §2 — HEAL% = 1.00, NOT 0. 'a multiplier on ALL healing received; base 1.0, so lifesteal and heals work with no modifiers. +35% Healing Received => x1.35.'

THORNS.description: 05 §2 — THORN = 0.00, the fraction of damage taken that is reflected.

wardCapPct.description: 05 §4.1 — the ward absorb pool is capped at this fraction of the actor's Max HP as it stood after 18 §8 step 7 (post-multiplier, pre-STAT_SET). Reading the post-step-7 value is what keeps CP_GLASS_HEART's re-based shields functional (18 §9.1). A grant that would exceed the cap is clipped. 05 §4.1 says explicitly: 'Lives in combat_caps.json.'

pvpMaxFightSeconds.description: 11 §4.3 — 'Duration cap: 60 s of simulated time — a PvP-specific override of the simulator's 90 s default (05 §3), set as pvpMaxFightSeconds in data/combat_caps.json.' ⚠️ The 90 s PvE default is deliberately NOT in this file: 05 §3's table carries no 📐 marker, so nothing authorises it as a tunable and inventing a key for it would be a number nobody agreed.

mitigation.description: 05 §4 — mitigation = effDef / (effDef + flatConstant + perLevelConstant * attacker.Level). 05 §4: 'the 120 and 20 constants are the two most important balance dials in the game. Expose them in data.' The same two dials are 29 §2.3's MitigationVsReference and already live at tuning/power_model.json#/mitigation; a DeclaredRules Mirrors rule fails the build if the two copies disagree.

perLevelConstant.description: 05 §4 / 29 §2.3 — the 20 term, multiplied by the attacker's Level. 05 §4: 'defense must keep growing to stay relevant — this is intentional.'
